method: Static PE extraction, pefile, Rizin and instruction-level data-flow review; samples were not executed.
external_context: Supplied Triage report URLs were inaccessible. ML labels, archive names and AV labels were not used as behavioral proof.

evidence: Entry CRT calls 0x401cb0; configuration dword 0x404120 is 3, selecting 0x401900 followed by self-delete routine 0x401390.
0x401900 constructs Active Setup Installed Components key and StubPath, reads its own image through CRT I/O, patches a copy, writes it and calls CreateProcessA.

Alternate installation branch 0x401260 deletes and replaces LanmanServer ServiceDLL. 0x401150 creates a target process, allocates and writes the DLL path remotely, resolves LoadLibraryA and supplies it as CreateRemoteThread entry.
0x401390 gets its own module path and short name, builds COMSPEC /c del and creates a process.
Resource PE at 0x5060 has Storm DDoS DNS and STORM command-format identifiers, but its declared entry bytes and import directory are zero, with no executable section.
samples.limits: Surviving malicious installer code establishes intent; successful installation, injection, DDoS operation and active C2 are not established. The resource image is damaged. Deployment provenance is unknown.

samples.identification: Gh0st-derived RAT / KernelYK NtHook driver installer
evidence: Main 0x401c30 enumerates guest-agent process names and branches to a VM reporting/exit path. This is a real probe, not inference from names alone.
0x401450 writes embedded kernel driver at file 0xba50. 0x401770 calls CreateServiceW with service type 1 and demand start 3, retains the handle in ESI and calls StartServiceW.
The kernel driver entry reaches 0x1586c then 0x15262, which writes safemon.dll, configures hooks, and adds NtHook.sys, safemon.dll and configuration filenames to its hide list.

Driver syscall dispatch 0x13d7e routes directory queries to 0x1334a. That handler calls the original query, filters names and compacts NextEntryOffset records or returns STATUS_NO_MORE_FILES to hide selected files.

Driver data file offsets 0x6bd0..0x6d40 contain real-mode boot code: reserve low memory, relocate, replace IVT INT13h, call the saved read handler, scan the loaded sectors and patch a far call to the relocated payload.

Embedded RAT at 0x147d8 contains Gh0st manager RTTI and hook/hook2 exports. At 0x1000e290 it polls key states in a loop and records translated keys with foreground titles. 0x1000e050 constructs the log filename on the stack, XORs each byte with 0x62 and passes the transformed buffer to the file write.
0x10010a30 dynamically resolves OpenClipboard/GetClipboardData, requests CF_TEXT, locks and copies text into a tagged buffer and passes that buffer to a helper.
Outer WinExec receives rundll32.exe safemon.dll hook2. The missing comma means this command text alone proves neither a valid export invocation nor a shell.
samples.limits: Input recording and kernel concealment tip the verdict. No authorized administration context was provided; OS compatibility, runtime success and current endpoint activity are unverified. Embedded boot-hook code is not proof of a successful MBR installation.

samples.identification: Same Gh0st / KernelYK installer with altered decorative bytes
samples.relation: Differs from b35753a34ae1 in 64 bytes in DOS-stub text and resource text only. All four embedded PE hashes and executable code are identical. The same traced behavior and limitations apply.

trait_changes.change: Remove artificial size gate from CreateServiceW import and retain import-based suppression of the duplicate name reference. Update neutral driver API profile to accept either evidence source.
trait_changes.consumer_audit: Other import consumers: resource-service-imports retains its own size gate; reversed-native-api-service-profile still requires reversed API and opaque writable data. Go runtime resolution consumer remains name-specific. sslip bootstrap is not broadened.

trait_changes.change: Retire pe-rundll32-dll-export-invoke from shell/script-host. Raw command text does not establish shell parsing or a valid DLL export call. WinExec and rundll32 executable references remain.
trait_changes.consumer_audit: No exact-ID consumers. Intentional removals: shell-execution-comp and data-heavy-shell-api-profile on these native installers. Other script-host descendants remain.

trait_changes.change: Consolidate uppercase IE executable-name metadata into case-insensitive process/info/name::iexplore-exe-name. Preserve scripts/binaries scope and update the Elex exact-ID consumer.
trait_changes.coverage_change: Lowercase and mixed-case spelling now match in the old uppercase rule scope. This is neutral executable-name evidence; it asserts no launch or browser theft.
trait_changes.consumer_audit: No selectors of the retired application-name ancestor. Existing process/info/name consumers select names or narrow IDs; this adds only IE case variants.

trait_changes.change: Add notable demand-start kernel-service create/start code detection, binding both call operands to actual imports and checking service type/start mode.
trait_changes.generalization: No chosen payload, service name, C2, sample hash, fixed file offset or file-size gate in the detection. Bound .text calls and Windows constants provide evidence.

controls: check.py uses ten static mutation controls. It checks kernel versus user service, demand versus auto start, both IAT bindings, missing start, import versus API-name text, file-size independence, rundll32 comma syntax and executable-name removal.
rescans: All three requested paths rescanned with atomscan after trait edits. All supported hostile findings retained; false shell and import-name findings removed.
